_about: Who has described an optimisation loop for inference, one line each. An entry needs either a signal (it has been weighed against the thesis) or a url (noted, not yet weighed). 'when' is when it was first described; 'updated' is a later post that matters. recent_from sets what the front page shows before 'show all'. Every sweep checks for teams missing from this list.

entries.gist: A coding agent built an LLM engine on a cloud FPGA for a ternary model, then sped it 33x over its own first build, spending $10k on tokens.
Agents run 24 to 30 hour hillclimbs on production vLLM. Winners ship and go upstream. A fully self-running loop is the stated goal, not yet built.
Parallel agents rewrite the engine's forward pass for a given traffic shape, model and chip, and recompile as traffic drifts.
An off-the-shelf coding agent found three kernel fixes for agent traffic in SGLang and topped the public benchmark with no production traffic.
One agent with a persistent knowledge base writes kernels for a datacenter GPU, a phone GPU and a RISC-V chip.
A customer-service AI company runs the loop on its own endpoints. Sub-agents must make a prediction that could fail before a change is kept.
A multi-agent loop taught itself a thinly documented NPU and its Rust DSL, then sped up three decode kernels about ninefold.
Agent-written kernels merged for one model on one chip. Proposes that reviewers judge evidence, since patches now outrun reading.
Agents rewrite a whole small engine across chained sessions that inherit their own notes, including the wrong ones.
A coding agent with a standing goal built a custom engine for one model in about a week. Not serving production traffic.
Not an agent loop. A controller re-splits the cluster as traffic shifts; no code is written. Listed because it sits under the same RSI label.
One agent implements, another reviews, and a profile must explain a gap first. Agents now produce most merged pull requests.
Profiles live deployments in 30-second windows, matches 35 known kinds of waste, and has agents implement and test fixes for expert review. Most fixes bought 3 to 6%.
A GLM-powered agent brought a GLM model to production on domestic accelerators. The authors say it is not yet RSI.
An agent tunes the whole serving stack for ads models, from kernels to the model server. Recommenders, not LLMs.
A language for describing inference workloads so an agent can search whole architectures, with an evaluator that needs no implementation.

entries.kind: Industry serving team, affiliation not stated
entries.gist: An internal harness runs SGLang work as agent task loops with fixed contracts and gates. Up to nine ran at once; verification caught a fake 5.7% kernel win.
Says its agents beat vLLM by up to 16% on eight GPUs. No code and no outside check.
An agent ports models to less common accelerators by following a costed map of routes. Baseten's engine run built on it.
Published skills let a coding agent port a new model into its engine. The kernels underneath stay human-written.

entries.who: NVIDIA Research and MIT HAN Lab
entries.gist: A contract, plan and verify workflow for coding agents on CUDA kernels. Took the top three places in the MLSys kernel contest.
Agents build a whole serving stack per model, chip and workload. Ties general engines in the common case, wins in unusual ones.
An autoresearch loop pointed at llama.cpp. Small CPU gains, nothing upstreamed, and most experiments failed.
Tree search over kernels across NVIDIA, AMD and in-house chips; search traces train the next model. Ads ranking, not LLMs.
An evolutionary kernel agent. Its kernels were merged into two engines and were worth about 1% end to end.
A coding agent replaces the mutation step of evolutionary search. A week of it beat vendor attention kernels by a few percent.
Pointed an autoresearch loop at fitting a trillion-parameter model on consumer GPUs, not its own cloud. Left alone, the agent drifted to its own question.
The first multi-agent system for GPU kernel optimisation, starting from SGLang's own kernels: 1.32x on average.
Claimed 10 to 100x from an agentic CUDA pipeline, then walked it back: the system had been gaming its own evaluation.
Hyperloom profiles a vLLM or SGLang server, searches settings and agent-written kernels, keeps only end-to-end wins, and stores recipes; a median 1.73x over stock on AMD chips.
An agent profiles an inference script, writes kernels for its dominant phases and keeps patches only if the whole model speeds up. 3.9 to 7x over eager PyTorch.
